### New-vote deferral primitive, 2026-10-28 — historical handoff

Implemented `meta::vote_admission::VoteDeferral` as an in-memory, store-instance/
representative/epoch scheduling guard. Acquisition serializes with reservations
through the existing LMDB writer, without committing a metadata row. New scalar
and batched reservations consult the same central guard; cached response checks
and a repeated existing final choice remain allowed. Existing epoch/deadline/
conflict/durable-fence checks still run, and the durable fence wins over deferral.
Nested guards reference-count ownership; drop/unwind releases only that owner.
No active guard costs one atomic read and no extra mutex/address allocation.
This is not a cross-process lock, signature authorization or persistent fence.

### Recovery caller review after152

Read-only continuation traced the actual production caller, not only the simple
rewind wrapper. `node/src/fork_resolution.rs` calls
`rollback_plan::stage_with` for admission evaluation and elected installation.
`stage_with` consumes descendant-first journals through
`rewind_block_with_snapshots` one at a time, then calls the candidate callback.
The production callback restores payment engines after that loop. A branch
containing a Merge and a verification transition therefore does not by itself
combine topology and revocation changes into one inverse journal.

When a graph inverse cannot retain the cache, `finish_trst_rewind` leaves it
absent. Later rewind iterations return early from `prepare_trst_rewind` when
that cache is absent; they do not each reconstruct all TRST state. The subsequent
`payment_transition::restore` calls `read_trst_engine`, which performs checked
wallet/graph reconstruction on a cache miss. This source trace rules out a
full-state reconstruction per remaining journal in this reviewed loop; it does
not establish a time/memory bound or prove all generic callers avoid fallback.
The public replacement callback remains general and must not be inferred safe
solely from the production callback review.

Also inspected the retained inverse's pending-basis guard: warm validation uses
`basis_validation_changes`, reverse origin/revision indexes and dirty rows.
It is not an unconditional scan of every pending row. Cold initialization still
decodes the pending table, and a large affected dependency set still costs work.
Existing `pending_revision_basis_scaling` and retained-graph recovery drivers
cover these distinct questions. Ledger reconciliation found that the same mixed
journal caller review was already recorded with the October21 pending work;
this continuation confirms that disposition rather than claiming a new fix.
The existing pending diagnostic covers100/1k/10k/100k rows: zero unrelated warm
row decodes, exactly one dirty-row decode, orphan rejection and cold reopen.
Its latest diagnostic parent is
`/home/burst/complexity-pending-revision-basis-corrected-20261021/scale-receipt.json`;
recorded100k cold construction2.053s and median warm validation0.025645ms are
historical scoped measurements, not current full-node qualification. Preparation
was already moved into startup and confirmed projection with component/node
passes. Do not schedule that implementation again. Distinct dependency fanout,
large affected sets and current full-node cold recovery remain separate gaps.
Before reusing this old result for a current claim, verify its receipt inputs;
no fresh receipt verification or runtime test was performed in this review.
No generalized inverse or new driver is justified by this trace.

## Prior handoff 139: concurrent external RPC load driver

`validate_network --load SECONDS REPORT FIRST_PUBLIC_SEED ACCOUNTS URL URL [...]`
now runs bounded concurrent Burn/Receive producers after the existing real-work
preflight. It uses SDK state, prepared work and local block/signature construction;
the production SDK still waits for finality in its ordinary submission API. Each
producer waits for exact admission before advancing its chain. A separate observer
requires every peer's confirmed height and exact signed block payload. At most1024
blocks remain in flight; deadlines stay25s. All signed attempts are logged before
transmission; ambiguous responses fail without automatic resubmission. Both sides
are joined, producer failures abort/drain remaining workers, and observer failure
closes its channel/releases permits. Final accounting checks complete pairs, exact
heads/counts/burn/TRST totals, unchanged stakes/representatives and signing authority.
Work/preparation, acceptance, all-peer observation, observer overhead and total drain
are separate evidence fields. RPC observation latency is an upper bound, not a
precise internal cementation timestamp. URL count does not establish host identity.

## Required consistency boundary

Initial retirement needs one authenticated **historical storage view** and complete
mutation coverage from that view until publication. Authenticate snapshot/certified
history, inventory origin, account tails, applied ordering, economics and rollback
requirements against the same view. Subsequent writes may add conservative
protection; they cannot grant eligibility to new candidates. Publication must still
reconcile covered writes and recheck the live writer cut atomically with deletion.

A consistent view is not authority by itself. All existing signature, certificate,
body digest, account-chain, economic replay, journal and rollback checks remain.
An arbitrary old projection plus a newly opened reader is not a consistent view.

| Stage | Current source and dependency | Required change / invariant |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recovery source | `snapshot/installed/metadata.rs::recover_metadata` opens a source reader for snapshot commitment and epoch | Capture source identity and mutation coverage at the same writer boundary; later epoch/layout changes reject the attempt |
| Tail planning | `SnapshotContinuation::plan_installed_tails` reads live account heads before witness acquisition | Plan both tails from captured heads; asynchronous witnesses must authenticate those exact hashes |
| Physical inventory | `snapshot/installed/retained.rs::InventoryCapture::advance` opens a fresh reader per page and checks the original cut | Page through one captured logical view with existing row/byte/digest/cardinality checks and bounded work; do not silently mix generations |
| Account planning | `retained.rs::plan` checks another fresh cut and captures AccountInventory | Use the same captured view as inventory and tail heads |
| Applied order/economics | `metadata.rs` reads ordering, replays owned inputs, then opens another writer for materialization and comparison | Replay and comparisons must agree on the captured ordering and economic rows; no writer held during replay |
| Journal authority | `JournalGuard::capture` depends on recovered accepted history and stored signer/journal bytes | Authenticate against captured records; preserve accepted-path versus installed-epoch distinction |
| Final guard | `RecoveredInstalledMetadata::verify_unchanged` checks inventory, journals, applied state and economics | Keep complete comparisons, directed at the captured view; separately prove live mutation coverage rather than pretending captured state is current |
| Root construction | `BodyRequirements::collect_with_projection` combines live references, applied archive and replay-derived provisional changes | Every source must be from the captured proof/view; rollback completeness cannot come from raw local undo images |
| Closure/classification | `ClosedBodyRequirements` requires rollback proof; `own_retirement` classifies original inventory | Keep authenticated prefix membership and complete closure.049covers later classification mutations, but an initial capture needs an earlier observation owner |
| Live publication | `OwnedRetirement::reconcile_until` and `OwnedPage::commit_counted` | Preserve bounded observations, conservative protection, epoch/layout invalidation, exact own-commit identity and atomic count publication |

Paths in the table are under `node/src/confirmed_replay` unless otherwise noted.

## Existing cache does not provide this boundary

`projection_cache.rs::ProjectionCache::get` rechecks cemented/applied tails,
inventory, economics and ordering against a live writer. It invalidates a changed
projection. `ProjectionCache::replay` supplies a starting point, explicitly requiring
`ReplayCache::recover` to recheck durable records. `CommittedProjection` carries
replay/projection state but no historical storage reader or mutation observation
covering the interval since publication. Therefore returning a stale cache entry
without these checks would change its security contract.

A future atomic publication handoff could be valid only if it retains the complete
root/rollback proof and installs observation coverage before releasing publication.
It must work for later epoch changes and restart/overflow recovery, not just initial
node startup. Current node startup launches initial tasks before starting retirement;
merely preparing before those tasks would not fix an already-running capture or
subsequent reinitialization. It is not a substitute for the failed048requirement.

## Rejected shortcuts

- Removing inventory/account comparisons or accepting mixed-generation pages.
- Treating stored BlockUndo beforeimages as authenticated rollback dependencies.
  The current root collector deliberately protects their carriers but requires
  replay-derived changes; closure rejects missing rollback proof.
- Holding payment publication exclusion or a native writer across full recovery
  and peer waits. This trades maintenance starvation for payment stalls.
- Copying the whole database without a bounded storage/cancellation and cut-identity
  contract. The installed heed copy API opens its own snapshot internally; it does
  not by itself associate the output with the caller's detached storage cut. Extra
  copied storage also cannot bypass the shared scratch policy.
- Extending timeouts, reducing arrival pressure, adding a quiet drain phase, or
  restarting048unchanged. None changes the failed consistency dependency.

##067native allocation diagnosis

The source has shutdown checks and individual witness deadlines (120+5seconds),
but no total capture deadline or live native-map growth/headroom guard. Economic
replay, full metadata verification and root construction also have synchronous
stretches checked only at their stage boundaries. A peer timeout alone cannot bound
the pages retained during capture.

The new bounded test in `store_lmdb/src/read_view.rs` compares identical96overwrites
of one128KiB value with/without an old reader, using an8MiB map and the existing
65536-row/64MiB observation policy. Unpinned completes96writes in363800us with
450560B file/allocated extent. Pinned completes54writes before precise MapFull in
356277us, reaching8314880B file/8318976B allocated extent; observation coverage is
still valid and the original snapshot remains intact. After dropping that reader,
96more writes succeed at the same map size and high-water extent. The failed write
left the latest committed value intact. This proves the observer/scratch budgets do
not protect ledger write capacity from a retained reader.

Build14.46s and4read_view cases pass; the resource diagnostic takes1.531725s. These
are small native-storage measurements, not payment latency or power-loss evidence.
The test deliberately expects the known capacity failure; its pass must not close
production readiness. No production code changed and no node rebuild was needed.

Next implementation must couple capture cancellation to native allocation/headroom
as well as a total lifetime limit, including peer/durable-cache waits and bounded
synchronous phases. Timeout alone is disproved by the sub-second exhaustion above.
Do not reinterpret observer bytes as native page bytes, or file length as allocated
filesystem blocks. A sampled cooperative guard has overshoot from in-flight writes
and non-interruptible work; identify and bound that exposure before claiming a hard
resource guarantee. Preserve one captured view, authenticated rollback/closure and
joined cleanup; silently reopening readers would restore the mixed-view failure.
An unchecked full database copy would merely move the missing resource budget.

##068cooperative capture budget implementation

The capture worker now has a local ShutdownController linked to parent shutdown.
Its durable-cache sessions and witness waits receive the local controller. A10ms
monitor checks elapsed time and native file high-water extent; exhausted budgets
signal that local controller and await the owned blocking worker. Headroom refusal
occurs under the initial clean writer before opening a native reader. Checks before
and after catalogue transfer prevent an over-budget completed catalogue escaping.
Storage errors racing cancellation remain errors. Neither the monitor nor the reader
is detached; a local budget stop does not shut down the node.

The local config defaults/ceilings are120seconds and64MiB extent growth, with a4MiB
minimum/default conservative remaining-map reserve. Operators can tighten them.
These are mitigation thresholds, not a proven production envelope. Extent includes
reusable pages, so a high-water database can conservatively decline capture even
when freelist space exists. `non_free_pages_size` opens another native reader and
walks database statistics; substituting it inside this pinned thread is invalid and
would not establish oldest-reader capacity anyway.

##071/072exact captured-view reuse

Implemented a separate verified_view cache on RecoveredInstalledMetadata. It is
filled only after every existing verify_view guard succeeds. Later captured checks
compare exact weak environment allocation identity and transaction generation;
dirty views have no clean cut and cannot match. The live writer verified_cut is
unchanged and is never populated by captured verification. No transaction is kept
alive by either cache. A failed newer-view verification leaves the old historical
proof intact without qualifying the failing view.

CleanStorageCut::same_committed_view intentionally differs from body dependency

### Next coherent change: compare captured keyed governance without a second engine

The expected GovernanceEngine is already authenticated replay output. Its existing
visit_records visitor emits every persisted logical record, including pending effects,
empty vote buckets, timings and key ballots. GovernanceRecord derives full typed Eq;
all GovernanceEngine fields participate in serde and its record representation.
Use this existing visitor, not another exporter or a newly buffered inventory:

1. Check the current keyed format and reject mixed aggregate/keyed storage using
   governance_storage's existing format validation.
2. Preserve the existing canonical expected-state validation and64MiB encoding bound
   with encode_into to a sink. Do not silently remove that existing guard while
   changing comparison strategy. This still has a full expected CBOR tree cost;
   eliminating it is a separate contract/review, not claimed here.
3. For each expected record, poll cancellation, derive its exact storage key, read
   from the same pinned view, run GovernanceRecord::from_storage_entry, and compare
   typed values. This retains row size/version/key/content/trailing-byte validation.
   Do not compare raw encodings: typed equality preserves logical collection equality.
4. Count all rows in the full governance namespace with fallible per-row checkpoints;
   exact expected count plus successful lookup of every unique expected key rejects
   extra, unknown and orphan rows without retaining a second key set. The expected
   visitor must emit unique keys; its representation and tests establish that.
5. Keep legacy aggregate and writer paths unchanged. Do not use this comparison to
   publish a reconstructed engine or skip ordinary storage-loader validation.

Matching the replayed bucket/pending records plus exact cardinality preserves the
current loader's structural checks. Test the new path against existing load_view +
canonical equality as an oracle, including missing/extra rows, wrong values, malformed
encodings, mixed/unknown formats, pinned old views after live corruption, and callback
errors. Extend existing governance-storage and capture fixtures. The change should
remove the *actual* GovernanceEngine/BTreeSet reconstruction and actual canonical
encoding, while expected canonical validation remains. Cost becomes expected visitor
work plus one DB lookup per record and one namespace count scan, with only one decoded
record retained at a time (pending effects can still be64MiB).

This is an implementation gap, not yet a passed optimization. BRN/TRST bulk restoration,
expected canonical tree, per-record work and native allocation overshoot stay open.
No additional runtime attempt is justified until that coherent diff and its assertions
are ready. Reuse080diagnostic and079functional evidence in their original scopes.

## Post-105 canonical allocation and nesting contract — October25

Read-only review; no protocol change, new runtime pass, or memory measurement.
All1007local source hashes still match105; its saved242-stage audit digest matches
and every recorded outcome passes in its original scope. Input hashes, including
locked ciborium0.2.2 sources, are saved in
`target/validation-evidence/signed-retained-closure-20261024/post105-canonical-review/source-review.json`.

`canonical::encode_at_depth` first writes the source representation through the
64MiB Bounded writer to a sink, then calls Value::serialized, then normalizes with
the supplied depth, then writes the normalized representation through another
64MiB bound. Both source and normalized byte limits are existing behavior. A
replacement must preserve both, not assume their lengths are always identical.

The locked dependency's value/ser.rs serialize_seq,serialize_map,serialize_struct
and tuple/variant paths allocate Vec capacity from declared lengths. Each element
recursively becomes a Value. Value owns strings,bytes,arrays,maps and boxed tagged
values. Our depth>64 check occurs after that construction. Map normalization also
holds encoded keys and a decorated sorting vector before collecting normalized
entries. Thus serialized byte size does not establish peak heap use,allocation
failure handling or a pre-allocation depth bound. No numeric amplification factor
is claimed without target-layout/allocator evidence. No remotely supplied arbitrary
Serialize implementation or observed production OOM has been demonstrated: typed
protocol reachability and worst admissible shape must be analyzed separately.

| Path | Current allocation/validation behavior | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Captured verification comparison,caches.rs |105borrows expected fields but generic encode_into still expands the full expected Value tree; actual values are102streamed fragments | Borrowing closes owned-map/prior-vote copies,not canonical tree memory |
| Captured governance comparison,caches.rs | Whole expected governance canonical guard then keyed actual comparison | Same remaining expected-tree issue; preserve full validity guard |
| Aggregate/writer comparisons,caches.rs | equivalent creates actual and expected canonical output Vecs sequentially; actual output lives through expected encoding | Output overlap remains distinct from Value-tree construction; not a reason to bypass full comparison |
| Committee publication,publication.rs | Retains actual snapshot and restored observation; canonical comparison still calls expected.snapshot |105borrowed view has not been applied here; publication must preserve certified-selection/event checks and atomic assignment |
| Checkpoint State encoding,snapshot.rs | Existing fieldwise writer streams accounts,pending,BRN wallets,blob maps,sequences,ordered histories and binary records | Reuse existing infrastructure; do not replace it with another full-State Value conversion |
| Unannotated checkpoint fields | verification,governance,BRN rates and other typed fields use generic Field encoding | Whole field trees remain even though the outer checkpoint is streamed |
| Large MapSource fields | >4096entries use sorted.rs,1MiB encoded-key batches and16KiB buffers; values are encoded one at a time to scratch | These are local buffers,not a process heap cap; one value/key and live merge runs remain relevant |

### Depth is part of the representation contract

Generic Field encoding starts at depth1. Existing Map and Sequence wrappers encode
children at depth2 because they are direct fields of the outer record. That is
correct for the current State field adapters. A verification record encoded at the
root has states-map values at depth2, but verification nested inside State has
those values at depth3. Reusing the current Map wrapper inside a new verification
field without carrying the parent depth would silently accept one extra level.
Spilled and in-memory branches must use the same inherited depth. Cached canonical
keys cannot reset depth, and unknown/newtype/tag representations must retain their
existing semantics. The existing tests cover current top-level boundaries,not a
new nested adapter automatically.

### Next coherent implementation boundary

Extend the existing field/map writer with explicit parent-depth propagation before
using it for nested verification fields. Keep the owned snapshot and105borrowed view
as byte/canonical oracles. Expose only read-only field/map views needed by the node;
do not make private economic state mutable or introduce a parallel decoder. Preserve
ordered prior votes/endorsements/sets and semantic selected/pool sequence order,
AttemptContexts,Neither history and skipped transient fields. Complete source-byte
and canonical-byte guards must remain; summing fragment bytes without adjusting map
headers/counts and nesting is not an established substitute.

Reuse and extend existing canonical fixtures: fieldwise_records_preserve_bytes_depth_and_invalid_value_rejection,
streamed_collections_preserve_headers_order_and_nested_depth,
streamed_maps_reject_distinct_keys_with_identical_encodings,and spilled-map duplicate/
value-failure cases. Add nested map/sequence boundary parity for in-memory and spill
paths before wiring a nested economic view. Node105canonical oracle and signed cases
remain valid for105; changed nested encoding needs the affected integration boundary.
Do not run unchanged capacity scenarios or infer a heap bound from the64MiB manifest.


## 106 inherited canonical depth implementation — October25

Field now accepts an explicit encoding depth. Generic serde fields normalize at
that depth; Map,BlobMap,Bytes,Sequence and OrderedSequence propagate it. Record
preflight carries the record depth to names and fields. Memory/spill map keys and
values receive the same child depth. Existing top-level callers retain depth0
record/depth1field/depth2child behavior and original byte limits. Empty collections
at depth64 are valid; no child at65 may serialize. Depth>64 is rejected before the
helper's own serialization, preventing usize overflow in depth+1. This does not
claim a pre-allocation guard for deeper nested generic serde values,whose Value
tree is still constructed before normalize descends through it.

Adapters without an explicit nested implementation (including current binary
record adapters) accept only the existing top-level field position; nested use
fails instead of silently resetting depth. No production nested binary use changed.
Nested economic views are not yet wired; this change provides the necessary safe
context for that next integration without changing schema or publication authority.
